newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rugby Union-Campese dumped to New South Wales reserves.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rugby Union-Campese dumped to New South Wales reserves.

text.p: Former Australia test winger David Campese was dropped on Monday by New South Wales for their opening fixture in the Super 12 rugby union competition.
Campese, who retired from test rugby three months ago with 101 caps and a world record 64 tries to his name, was relegated to the reserves bench to face New Zealand side Waikato Chiefs.
"You never know what's going to happen. I might only get five minutes, and to me that's not rugby," a dejected Campese said.
"You're always disappointed not to be in the 15. People say this will make me play a bit longer, but I just want to play for New South Wales and enjoy my rugby," the 34-year-old veteran winger said.
Campese was replaced on the left wing by Randwick teammate Chris Latham, who will make his debut for New South Wales at the Sydney Football Stadium on Saturday.

New South Wales coach Matt Williams said he fully intended to use Campese during New South Wales' opening fixture in the competition, which involves teams from Australia, New Zealand and South Africa and ends on May 31.
"People like Campo (Campese) are strike players. For a guy like him to come off the bench is invaluable to this team," Williams said.
Former Wallaby captain and front row forward Phil Kearns was also named on the reserves bench after being sidelined for the past 18 months by Achilles' tendon and knee injuries.
